name: Camellia
description:
{{nihongo|'''Masaya Oya'''|大箭将也|Ōya Masaya|born September 28, 1992|lead=yes}}, known professionally as {{nihongo|'''Camellia'''|かめりあ|Kameria|lead=yes}}, is a Japanese [[Electronic dance music|electronic]] musician and record producer. He is best known for his work in the [[rhythm game]] scene and has been a composer for games such as ''[[Sound Voltex]]'', ''[[Hatsune Miku: Project Diva]], [[Hatsune Miku: Colorful Stage!]]'' and ''[[Beatmania IIDX]]''. Outside of rhythm games, he has also worked with the record label [[Pony Canyon]] and is a member of the label EXITTUNES Dance Production (EDP), an imprint of [[Exit Tunes]]. He also publishes his discography on his [[doujin]] circle, KamelCamellia.

Oya began his career as a [[Vocaloid]] producer. Leaving the scene in 2013, he shifted his focus to primarily composing fast-paced [[electronic dance music]], with tracks often reaching or exceeding 200 [[Tempo|beats per minute]]. His music encompasses a variety of [[Electronic music|electronic]] styles, including [[J-core]], [[dubstep]], [[Denpa song|denpa]], [[drum and bass]], [[Hardcore (electronic dance music genre)|hardcore]], [[gabber]], [[Trap music|trap]], [[speedcore]], and [[doujin music]]. He is noted for actively experimenting with diverse sounds across his works, rather than adhering to a single genre.

He often collaborates with and has released several albums alongside the singer [[Nanahira]]. He has also produced remixes of the ''[[Undertale]]'' original [[soundtrack]] (OST) and collaborations with the game designer and composer [[Toby Fox]]. His track "Ghost" gained attention as one of the hardest songs in the [[Virtual reality|virtual reality (VR)]] rhythm game ''[[Beat Saber]]'' at the time of its release. He is popular outside of Japan through the video game ''[[osu!]]'', where he has a dedicated fan community. Oya is also an active [[Video game livestreaming|streamer]] on [[Twitch (service)|Twitch]].
